title: Attention Is All You Need
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp. 1–2, ending immediately before Section 2 Background. Read Section 4/Table 1, Section 5.2 and Section 6.1/Table 2.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: Avoid portraying the baseline as obsolete
Show why improvements leave an opening
Answer the bottleneck with a mechanism
Close with an empirical reason to care

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Removing recurrent dependencies changes available within-example parallelism; this is a structural argument before a benchmark claim.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The table compares layer-level operations; autoregressive inference still emits tokens sequentially, and quadratic attention cost remains.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Quality and training-time evidence accompany the mechanism rather than establish it.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The twelve-hour result is the base configuration; the larger headline model uses 3.5 days. Hardware, translation datasets and training recipes bound the comparison.

route_observation: Incumbent → dependency explanation → incomplete workarounds → reusable component → architectural removal → measured payoff. The practical question is implicit.
applicability: Useful when a design changes a specific dependency that readers can understand before implementation details.
counterexample_to_template: No contribution bullets, no explicit interrogative sentence, and only eleven Introduction sentences. A mandatory five-paragraph or question-list template would lengthen it. The second opening sentence is compressible if the citations add no distinction.
scientific_verification_limit: Body evidence and cost definitions checked; cited predecessors and empirical results were not independently reproduced.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, before Section 2 Related Work; visual order restored around Figures 1–2. Read §4.1/Figure 4/Table 2 and §4.2/Figure 6/Table 6.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: Make depth relevant to the audience
Give a reason to extend the trend
Convert a trend into an uncertainty
Open space for a different diagnosis
Name the problem at the right level

units.function: Describe the change in learning target
Report transfer to other vision tasks

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Higher training error challenges an overfitting account; an identity extension shows a no-worse solution exists without showing SGD will find it.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The diagnosis concerns these architectures and training settings. It is not a theorem about every deep network or every solver.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Residual fitting is motivated by an identity case, then supported by plain-versus-residual comparisons.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The optimization advantage is hypothesized and tested; parameterization alone does not prove easier optimization.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Depth gains motivate generality, but the stress test also supplies a boundary.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The 1202-layer model has worse test error than 110 layers. Vision transfer does not establish non-vision generality.

route_observation: Empirical anomaly → eliminate an explanation → constructive puzzle → explicit hypothesis → implementable mechanism → matched tests. One explicit question serves the anomaly.
applicability: Useful when a failure survives an obvious alternative explanation and a controlled comparison can diagnose it.
counterexample_to_template: The Introduction distinguishes an existence argument from an optimization hypothesis. Its final broad generality claim and repeated achievement language need qualification, not imitation; deeper does not universally mean better.
scientific_verification_limit: Read original diagnostic comparisons and the depth counterexample; no solver-theory proof or replication attempted.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
contribution_type: revitalized model family / objective connection / compression interpretation
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, before Section 2 Background. Figures 1–2 and embedded image metadata excluded. Read §3.2, §3.4, Tables 1–2 and §4.3/Figure 5.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: Equip readers to understand the opportunity
Prevent one metric from implying all
Turn a limitation into an analytical question
Broaden explanation without hiding the deficit

pivotal_transitions.warrant: The model family clears a sample-quality gap while remaining weaker on likelihood; the evidence supports a multi-metric claim.
pivotal_transitions.limit: Conditional and unconditional rows differ; likelihood upper bounds are not interchangeable with exact likelihoods. No universal dominance follows.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: The score-based connection motivates parameterization, and the objective ablation tests which combination produces quality.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The equivalence uses a specified parameterization; the simplified loss changes weighting. The table does not prove every diffusion formulation behaves similarly.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Rate/distortion decomposition explains why likelihood can look weak despite good samples.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The coding argument assumes a suitable sample-transmission procedure; it is not a measured production codec benchmark.

route_observation: Brief field context → define less-demonstrated family → quality result → technical connection → negative metric → explanatory interpretation.
applicability: Useful when the contribution combines a practical result and a mathematical reinterpretation, with conflicting metrics.
counterexample_to_template: No explicit question or contribution bullets. The limitation is central rather than relegated to the end. The broad first sentence could be shortened for an expert audience.
scientific_verification_limit: Equations, ablation and rate-distortion discussion inspected; proof derivations, samples and coding system were not independently reproduced.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, including the unnumbered Terminologies paragraph, ending before Section 2 Problem Statement. Figure 1 and footnotes excluded. Read §3, §3.1, Table 1 and §6.2/Table 4.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.function: Use model scale to show urgency
units.why_here: Turn inconvenience into a concrete constraint
Show the problem already has responses
Prevent efficiency alone from being enough

units.function: Mark low update rank as hypothesis
Explain memory relief through frozen states
units.why_here: Connect training cost to optimizer storage

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Low intrinsic dimension motivates, but does not entail, a low-rank update; rank ablations supply the empirical bridge.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3 equation (3), PDF p.3; §6.2 Table 4, PDF p.8
pivotal_transitions.limit: The table studies selected projections and tasks; rank-one sufficiency is not a theorem about all adaptation.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: A linear additive update can be merged into a fixed deployment weight matrix, meeting a stated latency constraint.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3 No Additional Inference Latency, PDF p.3; §3.1 limitations, PDF p.4
pivotal_transitions.limit: Merging concerns a fixed task. Task switching and mixed-task batching have separate costs; the paper itself discusses batching limits.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Frozen base weights remove most gradient/optimizer-state storage, while task-specific factors remain small.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3.1 Practical Benefits and Limitations, PDF p.4; §5 Table 1
pivotal_transitions.limit: Hardware and storage ratios are for the reported GPT-3 setup; they are not universal factors across optimizers or layer selections.

route_observation: Deployment constraint → competing trade-offs → explicitly labeled structural hypothesis → operational consequences → notation. Bullets inventory benefits, not a universal contribution format.
applicability: Useful when the method must satisfy several operational constraints simultaneously.
counterexample_to_template: The hypothesis is explicit rather than proven by an analogy. The final notation block is a legitimate local choice; not every Introduction must end with results. The advantages lead-in and small-matrix restatement are compressible.
scientific_verification_limit: v1 has seven authors and a narrower experimental roster than later presentations. Algebra, memory discussion and rank table checked; cited intrinsic-dimension studies and Appendix D not independently audited.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, before Section 2 Methods; Figure 1 excluded. Read §2.1–2.4, Tables 1–3, and §4.5 knowledge-update experiment on PDF p.10.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: Start from a useful existing capability
Derive a problem from that representation

units.function: Bound the scope of close predecessors
State the benefit of preloaded access

units.why_here: Test the promised expanded task scope
Report a competitive rather than best result

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Retrieval's inspectable memory is extended from extractive answers to generation through latent-document conditioning.
pivotal_transitions.limit: Retrieved passages provide access paths, not a guarantee that every generated claim is supported or faithfully attributed.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: A common interface is tested across distinct outputs; the results are not uniformly state of the art.
pivotal_transitions.limit: Generation metrics, human preferences and FEVER labels answer different questions. FEVER comparison involves supervision differences.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Replacing the index tests the earlier updateability motivation using temporally changed facts.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §4.5 knowledge-update experiment, PDF p.10: 82 changed heads of state, 2016 and 2018 indexes
pivotal_transitions.limit: This is a templated, bounded update demonstration with imperfect accuracy, not proof of globally consistent or reliable knowledge editing.

route_observation: Representational capability and liabilities → scoped predecessor → compositional mechanism → novelty clarification → multi-task evidence → motivation-specific demonstration.
applicability: Useful when composition is novel because of training regime or output scope, rather than wholly new components.
counterexample_to_template: No explicit question and no contribution bullets. A best-result template would erase the calibrated FEVER result. The pretrained-versus-from-scratch paragraph is necessary only if that distinction matters to the novelty claim.
scientific_verification_limit: Fixed v1 verified. Model definition, tables and update experiment read; retrieval provenance was not treated as proof of faithfulness and no results were reproduced.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–3, before Section 2; Figure 1 trajectories/caption and internship footnote excluded. Read §3 results/Tables 1–2 and §4/Tables 3–4.
segmentation_convention: All main-text sentences mapped; the four numbered contributions inside §1 P5.S1 are four statement units (a–d). Embedded dialogue and figure text are not separately counted.

units.why_here: Give the reader a concrete referent
Move from illustration to prior work
Explain a limitation of isolated reasoning

units.function: Identify missing abstract reasoning with exception

units.why_here: Converge both lanes on one uncertainty
Connect design to the motivating mechanism
Test the second half of the promise
Isolate the value of reasoning traces

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Interleaving gives a model channels for acquiring information and maintaining plans; the human example motivates rather than validates the design.
pivotal_transitions.limit: Verbal traces need not faithfully expose internal computation. Human cognition is an analogy, not causal evidence for LLM behavior.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: The results support conditional benefits and a hybrid strategy, while failure analysis reveals new failure modes.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3 Table 1/Figure 2; Table 2 and adjacent error analysis, PDF pp.5–6
pivotal_transitions.limit: ReAct is not best on every reasoning comparison; search failures and repeated reasoning loops remain. Small audited examples do not establish broad trustworthiness.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Action-only controls test whether explicit reasoning helps interactive tasks.
pivotal_transitions.limit: ALFWorld's headline uses best-trial comparisons; WebShop has its own evaluation protocol. Prompt selection and external-information access matter.

route_observation: Reciprocal everyday analogy → two asymmetric prior-work limitations → interleaving mechanism → task-specific comparisons → recap with future work.
applicability: Useful when two existing capabilities interact and each repairs a different limitation of the other.
counterexample_to_template: The opening example is explanatory, not obligatory. The recap largely repeats the previous paragraphs and may be cut under a tight budget. A universal superiority ending would contradict its hybrid-best result.
scientific_verification_limit: Evaluation tables and error analysis inspected; original cognition references, prompt-search robustness and trace faithfulness were not independently verified.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
contribution_type: hardware-aware algorithm with analysis and implementation
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–3, before Section 2 Background. Figure 1, labels, caption and code footnote excluded. Read §3.2 Theorem 2/Proposition 3 and Appendix C proof; §4.1 Tables 1–3; §4.3.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: State what an improvement should enable
Show why simple deletion is insufficient
Separate kernel evidence from model evidence
Explain why efficiency may affect quality

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Reduced FLOPs do not imply reduced wall time; IO traffic and hardware balance supply a different performance model.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3.2 Figure 2 and block-size experiment, PDF p.6; §4.3
pivotal_transitions.limit: At larger block sizes other bottlenecks intervene. The causal account is hardware- and shape-dependent, not a universal memory-only explanation.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: The IO upper bound is accompanied by a lower-bound claim whose quantifier matters.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3.2 Theorem 2/Proposition 3, PDF p.6; Appendix C proof, PDF p.23
pivotal_transitions.limit: Proposition 3 rules out an asymptotic improvement for all SRAM sizes; its proof uses the large-memory endpoint. It is not a tight pointwise lower bound for every size.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Kernel speed, end-to-end training speed and model-quality improvements require different evidence.
pivotal_transitions.limit: BERT comparison uses a target-accuracy protocol; GPT-2 speedup depends on baseline. Longer-context quality gains change the modeled context, while exact-kernel replacement alone preserves the model definition.

route_observation: Metric mismatch → hardware diagnosis → explicit design obstacles → paired algorithmic techniques → bounded theory → distinct levels of empirical payoff.
applicability: Useful when the community's proxy metric misses a real systems bottleneck and the proposed mechanism predicts a measurable reversal.
counterexample_to_template: The question is explicit, but the Introduction also supplies three pages of mechanism and caveats. Its end acknowledges faster approximate competitors. A single SOTA claim would erase the central distinction.
scientific_verification_limit: Original theorem statement and short lower-bound proof inspected, alongside experiment protocols; no independent proof audit, kernel reproduction or current-library speed comparison.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
contribution_type: workload diagnosis plus operating-system abstraction transfer
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, before Section 2 Background; visual column order restored around Figures 1–2. Figures, captions, ACM notice and footnote excluded. Read §6.1–6.3/Figures 12–15 and §7.1/Figure 18a.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: Connect token behavior and serving load
Ground the constraint in a configuration
Explain the memory object being optimized
Show why a usual tensor assumption fails
Connect length uncertainty to unused capacity
Show why an oracle is insufficient
Propose one response to both failures

units.function: Map OS analogy onto serving objects
Declare supported model and distribution scope
Report throughput while preserving model computation

pivotal_transitions.warrant: A memory budget and measured waste connect allocation policy to achievable batching and throughput.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: Figure 2, PDF p.2, linked to §6.2; Figure 13, PDF p.10; §6.1
pivotal_transitions.limit: Memory fractions are not universal constants. Orca is the authors' reimplementation with three reservation policies; workloads use dataset-derived lengths and synthetic arrivals.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: The transferred paging abstraction is justified by mapping each design property to a diagnosed failure.
pivotal_transitions.limit: Finite blocks still permit some internal waste, and sharing depends on common prefixes/decoding structure. The OS analogy alone supplies no performance proof.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: System throughput can improve despite a slower individual attention kernel.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The microbenchmark reports 20–26% higher attention-kernel latency. End-to-end gains depend on batching and memory pressure; short workloads with ample cache space reduce the advantage.

route_observation: Application cost → execution pattern → memory budget → two quantified allocation failures → paging mechanism → integrated system → workload-bounded evidence.
applicability: Useful when a resource layout constrains a higher-level objective and several failure modes share one abstraction-level solution.
counterexample_to_template: No explicit question is needed because the constraint chain supplies the problem. Contribution bullets repeat an already complete argument. The opening impact/cost rhetoric is less portable than the workload analysis.
scientific_verification_limit: Full Introduction and original evaluation assumptions checked. Economic estimate not re-audited; no independent serving benchmark or universal numerical equivalence claim.

title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, before Section 2 Programming Model. Original Google-hosted author paper marked To appear in OSDI 2004, not the later CACM article. Read §3.3 failure semantics; §5.3–5.5/Figure 3; §6/Table 1. USENIX page independently verified identity; direct download returned 403.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.function: Ground problem in repeated production work
units.why_here: Establish firsthand scope and workload diversity
Create the contrast that motivates abstraction
Show why a local solution is insufficient
Describe origin without claiming new primitives
Explain why simplicity can coexist with scale
Pair usability claim with performance obligation

pivotal_transitions.warrant: A repeated mismatch between simple computations and complex distribution motivates a small interface.
pivotal_transitions.limit: The pattern comes from Google's workloads. Adoption and code volume are experience evidence, not a controlled usability experiment or universal expressivity proof.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Functional operations permit re-execution, but failure semantics require explicit conditions and commit behavior.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §3.3 Semantics in the Presence of Failures, PDF p.5; §5.5/Figure 3c, PDF pp.9–10
pivotal_transitions.limit: Sequential-equivalent output assumes deterministic user functions. The fault test kills worker processes on functioning machines, not arbitrary correlated machine failures.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: System-level benefits need actual workload and failure experiments beyond the abstraction's elegance.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §5.3–5.5/Figure 3, PDF pp.8–10: normal sort, disabled backup tasks and killed workers
pivotal_transitions.limit: Sort uses a known key distribution, locality and replicated output. These settings bound timing comparisons; no blanket best-system claim follows.

route_observation: Firsthand repeated work → simplicity/scale mismatch → abstraction distilled from common structure → execution consequences → combined interface/system contribution → roadmap.
applicability: Useful for systems papers whose novelty lies in making a recurring engineering pattern usable and reliable.
counterexample_to_template: No explicit research question, no contribution bullets, and no opening SOTA contest. The six-sentence roadmap is optional navigation and a clear compression target; production adoption is not causal proof of ease of use.
scientific_verification_limit: Original 2004 author paper and publisher identity checked, with runtime/failure text inspected. No Google deployment access, benchmark reproduction or independent usability study.

title: Ray: A Distributed Framework for Emerging AI Applications
reading_scope: Full Section 1, PDF pp.1–2, before Section 2 Motivation and Requirements. Main-text visual column order restored; footnotes excluded. Read §2–3.2, §4.2.1–4.2.2, §6.1/Figures 7–9, §6.2/Figures 10–11, §6.3.3/Table 3.
segmentation_convention: Every main-text sentence in Section 1, in visual column order; captions, figure labels, footnotes and headings excluded. Pn.Sm means paragraph n, sentence m; explicit contribution clauses may have letter suffixes.

units.why_here: Locate relevance for a systems audience
Avoid making the motivation purely speculative
Show why static assumptions are awkward
Introduce latency as a distinct requirement
Show that throughput and latency coexist
Create a contract for the proposed system
State a response to the contract

units.function: Connect local decisions to latency and load

pivotal_transitions.warrant: The workload analysis makes graph flexibility, state and latency independent requirements, then assigns abstractions to them.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §2 RL pseudocode/requirements; §3.2 stateful edges, PDF pp.2–4
pivotal_transitions.limit: Representative RL workloads motivate the design; the broad forecast about all emerging AI is not established by these examples.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: Externalized control state and local-first scheduling are proposed mechanisms; scalability and recovery need separate experiments.
pivotal_transitions.source_locator: §6.1 Figures 7–8, PDF p.9; §6.2 Figures 10–11, PDF p.10
pivotal_transitions.limit: The headline throughput experiment is embarrassingly parallel. It does not establish linear scaling for every heterogeneous dependency graph.

pivotal_transitions.warrant: A latency-sensitive application tests whether measured runtime behavior serves the original use case.
pivotal_transitions.limit: This is simulated soft real time: the reported walk is stable at a 3 ms budget but not 2 or 1 ms. It is not a hard deadline guarantee for physical robots.

route_observation: Workload shift → derived system requirements → capability-specific predecessor mismatch → paired programming abstractions → state/scheduling architecture → contribution recap.
applicability: Useful when a new workload combines demands that existing systems satisfy only separately.
counterexample_to_template: No explicit question, and no numerical result in this Introduction's ending. Requirements and architecture carry the argument. The generic opening forecast is less evidentially secure than the concrete workload derivation.
scientific_verification_limit: Original v1 (2017, nine authors), not later OSDI revision, was analyzed. Key performance/recovery/application evidence checked; comparison set, runtime and fault model were not independently reproduced.
